candidate.blueprint_locator: Management of Care — quality improvement, incident/event review and patient safety systems
candidate.educational_objective: Differentiate voluntary external reporting of sentinel events from required internal safety learning and improvement expectations.

options.A: The organization should identify the event, examine root causes and contributing factors, and make improvements to reduce recurrence risk even if it does not report the event to Joint Commission.
options.B: Every sentinel event must be reported to Joint Commission because external reporting is mandatory.
options.C: The organization should delay internal analysis until Joint Commission requests it.
options.D: If the event is not reported externally, no formal internal improvement action is expected.

candidate.rationale: Joint Commission states that reporting sentinel events to it remains voluntary, while accredited healthcare organizations are expected to identify sentinel events, examine root causes and contributing factors, and make improvements to mitigate recurrence risk. Therefore A is correct.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Sentinel-event reporting to Joint Commission is voluntary, but accredited organizations are expected to identify events, examine root causes/contributing factors, and make improvements to mitigate recurrence risk.
